fatal_errors: The proposed plasma-nitriding treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention of atmospheric plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating followed by annealing at 550 °C.
It omits the target SS316L substrate, HEA coating composition, coating thickness, annealing step, and specified electrochemical and molten-salt environments.
The stated 400–500 °C range is overly broad: at the upper end, chromium-nitride precipitation can deplete chromium from the matrix and reduce rather than improve corrosion resistance.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general surface-modification problem and low-temperature plasma nitriding can plausibly improve corrosion behavior when expanded austenite forms without chromium-nitride precipitation. Its untreated control and polarization-based falsification experiment are reasonable, although the exposure environment and processing parameters are insufficiently specified. Scientifically, however, it is a different intervention with a different structural mediator and mechanism from the hidden target. It therefore recovers only the generic directional outcome of improved corrosion resistance and none of the target-specific HEA coating, 550 °C annealing optimum, passive oxide chemistry, hardness response, or hot-corrosion results.
